[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L5 adds gut-wall efflux and intestinal-metabolism experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for presystemic loss, with direction and experimental context preserved; mechanism alone is not a direct oral-bioavailability result.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Direct morphinan-analog F measurements are above the 20% threshold: morphine fasted tablet absolute F was 29.2 ± 7.2% vs IV (C08, C10); codeine sulfate absolute F was 80.5% (C07); codeine relative to IM was 50.2 ± 2.1% and 54.8 ± 4.9% (C19, C25, C39, C49); ethylmorphine systemic availability was median 0.74 (range 0.54-0.92) with a single-subject absolute F of 28% (C03, C06).

L4 provides affirmative intestinal absorption and solubility evidence for close morphinan analogs: codeine human fraction absorbed was >90% (C151) and codeine was classified as high solubility (C127); morphine sulfate and hydrochloride salts were soluble at 64.5 and 57.0 mg/mL, respectively (C126, C135).

L5 gut-wall evidence is favorable for the closest supplied analog: naltrexone (same 6-keto-14-hydroxy morphinan, N-cyclopropylmethyl instead of N-allyl) had Caco-2 Papp A-B 15.1 ± 0.6 ×10^-6 cm/s, Papp B-A 19.7 ± 0.5 ×10^-6 cm/s, and efflux ratio 1.3, indicating no net efflux (C174); morphine is a weak P-gp substrate, is rapidly absorbed from the small intestine (C167, C202), and is transported across Caco-2 at a much higher rate than mannitol/PEG4000 (C195); samidorphan, another morphinan, had Papp A-B 18.77 ×10^-6 cm/s (C203).
No supplied card provides a direct F measurement for the query or for naltrexone; C59 gives only an oral naltrexone Cmax without an IV comparator, so it cannot affirmatively establish F < 20%.

Intestinal UGT metabolism is documented for morphine (C169) and P-gp inhibition increased oral morphine exposure (C190), but morphine's direct F remains 29.2% (C08, C10), so these mechanisms are not affirmative evidence that the query falls below 20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule (N-allyl-6-keto-14-hydroxy morphinan) or for naltrexone, the closest supplied analog.
C59 provides only an oral naltrexone Cmax without an IV comparator, so it cannot be converted into an F estimate or used as affirmative evidence for F < 20%.

No first-pass hepatic metabolism or clearance data are supplied for the query; the 6-keto, 14-hydroxy, and N-allyl modifications may alter first-pass extraction, but this is not quantified in any card.
L4/L5 absorption, solubility, and gut-wall data come from morphine, codeine, and naltrexone, not from the query itself; transfer is inferred from structural similarity.
content.decision_summary: Prediction remains high because all direct morphinan-analog F measurements are above 20%, L4 adds favorable absorption/solubility evidence, and L5 shows the closest analog naltrexone has good Caco-2 permeability with no net efflux; no affirmative threshold-relevant evidence supports F < 20%. Confidence stays low because no direct F or first-pass data exist for the query's specific N-allyl-6-keto-14-hydroxy morphinan.

messages.content:
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L5 adds gut-wall efflux and intestinal-metabolism experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for presystemic loss, with direction and experimental context preserved; mechanism alone is not a direct oral-bioavailability result.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

{"protocol":{"version":"conditioned_gold_context_records_plus_stage3_l3_l5.v1","mode":"progressive update","architecture":"The same ten exact training parent-condition contexts remain visible. L1 contains current-gold constituent measurements. L2 appends other raw gold-source-domain records from those same contexts; all L1 cards remain visible. L3, L4, and L5 append one ranked Stage 3 record bundle each; all earlier cards remain visible.","record_sampling":"Each context and level shows a deterministic sample of at most ten raw records. available_record_counts reports the full pool before sampling. Repeated records and records from one context are not independent votes.","level_interpretation":"L2 records did not contribute a current gold vote. That does not make them negative, invalid, or independent votes; use them only as additional experimental context. L3-L5 are separately retrieved mechanistic families, not additional gold votes.","transfer_rule":"transfer_likelihood estimates whether a training context applies to this query.
